doc.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022

title: Roberta Flack and Elliot Lawrence's Kennedy Center Honors gigs
summary: Meeting a drummer at a Flack date; Elliot Lawrence's studio and Kennedy Center work.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. I’m enjoying it. It’s great. Great hang, man.
Yeah, and some of these acts like Cher and Roberta Flack, was it a memorable experience or just one more day?

Roberta Flack was nice, yeah. That was I got to meet — oh it was a great drummer. I was on a couple of tracks and he was on another track. He’s a great player, oh I forgot his name. Anyway we hung out a while. I hung out with this drummer a lot on the gig. But you know playbacks, you’d sit together and talk. But yeah, there were some great experiences man. Like you know what I got to do that I really loved man, I used to do all of Elliot Lawrence’s work you know. I don’t know if you remember Elliot Lawrence.

Years ago we had a jazz band, a great jazz band. Anyway he became a producer in New York and I was on everything he did. And soaps, films, he did all music and sometimes he would use Torrie, I’d see Torrie. Torrie would come in with the music. I’d say, “Oh hey man” you know. But the gigs that I did he used to take a band like you would take a rhythm section to Washington and we’d do the Kennedy Center man, you know the Kennedy Center Honors. And it was such a great gig man. And I did about five of them, © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

five or six of them. Clinton, Bush, who else? Reagan. Now was it, no I didn’t do Reagan. I don’t know if it’s right. Anyway after the gig we’d go to a dinner you know and all of that. I’d take my wife you know. It was really, really a beautiful experience man. That was a great — and then he lost it, Elliot lost it. Another conductor came in. Of course they used their guys. You know. But it was a great gig. The orchestra was great you know, always. And we’d rehearse. We’d go in, we’d pre-record a lot of it there, right there you know. But that was a great gig. And we’d do the Ford Theater and there’d be a benefit for the Ford Theater every year and that was great because the president and everybody, the cabinet, you know it’s a tiny theater. They were all sitting down front on top of us. We were on stage and I’m looking at Bush and this one and that one. Jeez, it was fantastic. That was fantastic. But then he lost that gig too. Everybody got older you know, we get older and new people come in and they’re great. There are so many drummers around man, I can’t believe it, that just blow my mind man.
Blow my mind. I’m like how does he do that? It’s amazing.
